\subsection{RQ3/E3：机制隔离和 actionability}

RQ3 检验 profiler 是否能通过 operation fields、operation-stack depth、mapping/tagging rules、ranking policies、profile specs 和 boundary-derived operation fields 暴露 actionable optimization knobs。
Hidden labels 仍然只在 profiling 之后用于 scoring，boundary-derived fields 还用 held-out OSWorld-Human boundary positives 评分。
我们比较 default semantic-width specs、patched specs、visible feature rankers、transfer policies、learned-boundary stacks、fixed-session 和 semantic-width stacks，并报告 accepted patches、AP delta、top-5 lift delta、first-positive-work delta、group reduction 和 top-5 work counterpoint。
OSWorld-Human 需要 boundary-derived fields，这说明 RQ3 评估的是可操作机制证据，而不是自动边界发现或自动 patch 选择。
这一节的问题是 localization gain 来自哪些机制，以及 profile-guided 的 operation fields、operation-stack depth、rank features、mappings 或 boundary-derived fields 能否在不把 hidden labels 泄漏进 profiler input 的前提下改善输出。
Rank-feature、mapping、stack-depth、boundary-field、profile-spec patch、case view、diagnostic lens 和 transfer counterpoint 共同支撑同一个 RQ3 claim。

主要机制问题是：E2 的 ranked groups 能不能解释应该怎样改 profile configuration。
Hidden labels 只在 profiling 之后用于 scoring；visible inputs 仍然是 operation fields、operation-stack depth、mapping/tagging rules、rank features、profile specs 和 boundary-derived operation fields。
成功条件是 actionable、replayable diagnosis：每个任务应该指向具体的 operation field、stack depth、ranker、mapping、profile-spec 或 drilldown change，并且 executable patches 能改善 scored output，但不能把结果写成 automatic selector。

表~\ref{tab:actionability} 是 E3 的主显示，它把 task-level localization signal 转成 diagnosis table。
SATraj unsafe 说明 \texttt{environment,phase,action} 和 risky/write-action ranking 对安全问题有效；looping 说明 \texttt{repeat\_signal} 有用但需要 prevalence-aware ranking；side-effect 指向更深的 write/input mapping；AgentNet step-quality 需要 action-family 定位后再进入 fixed-session examples；OSWorld-Human 则需要 boundary-derived fields。
因此 actionability 的第一层结论是：profiler 指出该调 operation field、stack depth、mapping、ranker、profile spec、boundary field 还是 drilldown，而不是给出唯一默认 view。
Task-level verdict synthesis 给出任务级结论：6/6 任务都是支持但有反例，不是无条件胜出。
其中 5/6 任务有 accepted executable profile-spec patch；剩下的 OSWorld-Human row 指向 boundary-derived fields，并保留 top-five 与 first-positive work 反例。
这 6 行进一步收敛成三类可复用优化模式。
Safety 和 side-effect 任务指向 field 与 ranker 修改，因为 environment、phase/action 和 write/input fields 会把相关 positives 推到更小的 inspected region。
Step-quality 任务指向 drilldown workflow，因为 desktop phase、repeat 和 action fields 先定位可疑区域，再由 fixed-session examples 解释单条 trace。
Human-boundary 任务指向 representation repair，因为 action-depth stack 不够，boundary-derived operation fields 能提高 AP 并减少 groups，但仍保留 inspection-work 反例。
这些模式给出的是 profile inputs、operation fields、stack depth 和 rankers 的配置建议，不是 profiler 自动预测出的标签。
Field-suitability decisions 进一步说明这些配置建议何时可用。
Deterministic mapping、stack depth 和 predicates、operation-level rank features、supervised boundary fields、boundary-profile repair 分别对应不同的 accept/caution/reject 条件。
因此 E3 的 actionability 是 profiler 指出该调哪个 operation-field 或 operation-stack view，而不是自动选择唯一正确视图或自动发现所有边界。
Automatic operation-stack induction 也落在这个 actionability 边界内。
它证明 profiler 可以从可见字段递归诱导 operation-only stack，并把深度参差的 stack 当作可打分 view，但它的 AP 反例说明 profile-specific stack 和 ranker 仍然需要按任务调优。
Depth sensitivity 把这点变成可操作结论：同一 induced profiler view 在 depth 3 取得最高 query-aware median AP，在 depth 5 取得最低 median top-5 work，而有 material split 的 task-level AP-best depth 跨 2、3、4、5 分布。
因此 E3 的建议是调 operation-stack depth 和 ranker objective，而不是把 \texttt{analysis\_task,phase,action,status} 当成固定 ontology。

机制消融说明这些诊断来自可复现的 profiler 配置。
Stack-text rank rules 和 rank mode 可以从 profile spec 复现，但它们对 safety/side-effect 过粗；operation-level rank features 在 folding 前匹配 visible mapped operation tokens，semantic stack 的 feature ranking 在 AP 上赢 5/6 tasks、top-5 lift 赢 4/6、first-positive work 赢 5/6，coarse depth 在 4/6 tasks 上改善 AP 并减少 groups。
Leave-one-feature 和 robustness analyses 说明哪些字段有用或有害：\texttt{repeat\_signal}、write-action 和 \texttt{status=success} 在不同 family 关键，SATraj loop-like 或 OSWorld-Human input-phase features 会误导；global/equal feature banks 常能保留收益，guided repair 在 2/3 misleading-feature cases 上改善 AP。
这些 repair 使用离线评分反馈，因此支持 mechanism isolation；它们不是自动 learned ranker，也不支持 automatic learned ranker。

View、depth 和 budget 审计把机制结果放回 profiling tradeoff。
Best AP 和 best top-5 F1 分散在 operation-stack、fixed-session、dataset-native、raw-action 和 flat views；leave-task source selection 不能稳定选中 best view。
但 operation-stack query-aware 在 6/6 tasks 上进入 Pareto frontier，相对 flat 在 6/6 tasks 降低 top-5 work，相对 fixed-session 在 5/6 tasks 提高 top-5 recall，并在 5/6 tasks 用更少 groups 达到 50\% positives。
25\% recall target 下它覆盖 6/6 tasks，median work 为 0.2000 而 flat 为 1.0000，median groups 为 16.0 而 fixed-session 为 50.0；50\% recall 和 first-positive work 仍保留 fixed-session、dataset-native 或 raw-action counterpoints。
Sequence-scope 和 oracle-depth 审计进一步说明：30\% work budget 下 positive-session recall 为 0.4669，高于 fixed-session 的 0.3230；24 个 oracle-depth rows 上 budget-30 positive-unit recall median 为 0.4342，并在 20/24 rows 提高 fixed-session unit recall、22/24 rows 用更少 groups 达到 50\% positive units。
Positive-run proxy units 是 episode-derived proxy units，不是 human intent；\texttt{positive-session-without-unit} fixed-session depth-gap counterpoint 仍然保留，所以这只是 depth-aware triage，不是自动发现所有 latent subtask 或 intent boundary。
多指标审计也保留反例：30 个 baseline-metric comparisons 支持 operation-stack query-aware，16 个是明确 counterpoints，nDCG 场景下 flat 或 dataset-native 可能胜出。

Actionability view 把这些比较变成可以检查的优化建议。
36/36 objective rows 都有具体 profile-configuration action，但 27/36 best visible policies 不是默认 operation-stack query-aware；transfer miss 多数对应 view 或 ranker 变化，而不是不可解释错误。
同一证据可以从 diagnostic lenses、case examples 和 baseline contrasts 三个角度检查：6 个 lenses 覆盖 36 objectives，top-5 case groups 在 6/6 tasks 命中 positive，top-1 在 5/6 命中，median top-5 lift 为 1.6508 且 work 为 0.0937；operation-stack 在 6/6 tasks 胜过 flat top-5 work、在 5/6 胜过 fixed-session top-5 recall，同时保留 fixed-session first-positive 和 flat full-recall 反例。
Visible counterfactual 和 held-out transfer results 把行动建议与目标标签泄漏分开：36/36 best rows 是 visible non-oracle，27/36 需要 non-default action，25/36 需要 view change；held-out action transfer 在 35/60 aligned decisions 上 within tolerance，但 exact action-class transfer 只有 7/60，在 non-default target action 上只有 2/42。
因此这里的 claim 是可调诊断 surface，不是 label-free automatic selector。

Executable profile-spec patches 关闭一个从诊断到可执行配置的闭环。
Default 与 patched profile specs 在同一 visible operation input 上实际运行 Rust \texttt{agentpprof --profile-spec}，hidden labels 只在 profiler 输出后评分；5/6 patches 同时改善 AP、top-5 lift 和 first-positive work，median AP delta 为 0.0376，median top-5 lift delta 为 0.5750。
这里的 failure interpretation 同样重要：唯一 reject 是 OSWorld-Human，说明 visible phase/action rank features 不足以处理 human-boundary 目标。
Held-out boundary-derived fields 随后作为普通 operation fields 折叠，AP 从 semantic-width 的 0.2402 提升到 0.2583，groups 从 108 降到 74；反例是 top-5 work 和 first-positive work 变差。
这些 patch 和 boundary-field results 支持 boundary-derived fields 是 actionable operation-field knob，不支持 automatic boundary discovery、automatic patch selector 或第五个核心实验。

\subsection{RQ4/E4：Replayability、离线成本和 scope control}

RQ4 问复现者能否重放支撑 E1--E3 的离线 profiler 输出，并看清哪些 claim 仍未被测量。
我们把 76 个 profile specs 和对应 operation inputs 当作复现单位，同时检查本地 session、agent-session trace 和 standard trace 这些输入来源是否都进入同一 folding path。
我们比较 default output 与 deterministic-output replay，比较 semantic profile hashes 与 raw-byte profile hashes，并验证声明的 input paths 是否实际进入 operation-stack folding path。

619	\section{数据源选择与扩展边界}
620	
621	当前数据选择遵循 oracle-first 原则。
622	Operation-stack profiling 的主 claim 需要有顺序、有动作、并且能隐藏评分标签的真实轨迹。
623	规模更大的数据集如果缺少这些字段，只能支撑覆盖范围，不能支撑 localization accuracy。
624	OSWorld-Human 提供 single-action 和 grouped-action，因此最直接支撑递归边界验证。
625	AgentNet 同时提供大规模人工桌面任务和 per-step correctness/redundancy，因此支撑 step-quality profiling。
626	AgentRewardBench 和 SATraj-OS 把评估目标从 action taxonomy 推到 failure、looping、安全和 side-effect diagnostics。
627	GUI-Odyssey、tau-bench 和 ToolBench 则作为跨域覆盖来源，说明 operation abstraction 可以覆盖移动 GUI、user-agent-tool dialogue 和 API/tool traces，而不局限于桌面轨迹。
628	
629	ScaleCUA 的作用是扩大 GUI history 覆盖，而不是提供新的主证据。
630	我们使用的 ScaleCUA stream sample 含 5,000 个 Ubuntu navigation rows，覆盖 131 个 sessions，最大 step 为 48。
631	该子集的 action taxonomy 主要是 click 和 terminate，所以 phase/action 指标达到 1.0 并不表示强泛化。
632	它更适合证明 multi-step GUI history context 可以被投影为 \texttt{history\_state} 和 \texttt{history\_depth} fields，而不是证明复杂边界 detector。
633	
634	\section{相关工作}
635	
636	\textbf{Profiling、flamegraphs 和 trace analysis.}
637	传统 flamegraph 和 pprof 路线把运行时调用栈折叠成热点视图~[1,16,17]。
638	pprof 不只是固定 call stack：它支持 sample tags，也支持用 \texttt{tagroot}/\texttt{tagleaf} 把 tag value 作为 pseudo stack frame 可视化~[17]。
639	Perfetto 则代表系统 trace ingestion、SQL trace analysis、trace summary 和 derived events 的成熟方向~[18]。
640	因此本文不能把 novelty 写成“只有我们支持 query-time aggregation”。
641	本文复用 folded-stack 表示，但 scoped novelty 是 agent-operation record model、recursive multi-field operation-stack projection 和真实标注轨迹上的 hidden-label localization benchmark 这三者的组合。
642	Stack frame 来自 agent operation fields，而不是语言运行时函数调用或通用 trace SQL schema。
643	因此同一批 operations 可以被折叠为 task、phase、tool、action、quality 或 safety 视图，也可以改成 fixed-session 或 flat baseline。
644	区别不在图形样式，而在 agent 语义对象、递归多字段 stack projection 和跨数据集 hidden-label scoring。
645	
646	\textbf{Agent tracing 和 LLM observability.}
647	OpenTelemetry GenAI 和 OpenInference 标准化 GenAI spans、LLM calls、agent reasoning steps、tool invocations、retrieval operations、MCP 和 provider-specific telemetry~[2,11]。
648	LangSmith、Langfuse、Phoenix 和 AgentOps 等系统进一步把 LLM call、tool call、latency、token、trace tree、session、observation、evaluation score、goal、plan 和 agent artifact 放进单次 workflow inspection 与生产监控~[12,13,14,15]。
649	这些系统是本文最接近的同问题相关工作。
650	因此本文把 trace/span/session 明确当作 exchange container 或 baseline shape，而不是加成第三个 profiler 抽象。
651	E2 实际评估的是 fixed-session drilldown 这个 trace-tree-shaped baseline；真实 OpenTelemetry/OpenInference/Phoenix span-tree import 仍是后续互操作 baseline，不是当前已完成结果。
652	本文关注跨轨迹 semantic profiling，把异构标注轨迹或本地 agent 历史统一为 operations，并允许用户选择 stack 深度、mappings、tagging 和 ranker。
653	因此本文把这些系统作为同问题 baseline threat，而不是声称替代现有 observability products。
654	
655	\textbf{Agent failure 和 span localization。}
656	2026 年的 AgentRx、TELBench/DRIFT、Holistic Evaluation and Failure Diagnosis 和 AgentAtlas 是最接近的同问题威胁~[23--26]。
657	AgentRx 发布带 critical failure step 和 failure category 的失败轨迹，并用 constraint checking 与 LLM judge 做 root-cause localization。
658	TELBench/DRIFT 把 deep-research agent 轨迹转成 semantic spans，并标注 harmful error spans。
659	Holistic Diagnosis 把 agent-level diagnosis 和 span-level evaluation 结合起来；AgentAtlas 则强调 outcome leaderboard 不能覆盖 trajectory quality 和 control-decision quality。
660	因此本文不能把 novelty 写成 failure localization、trajectory diagnosis 或 span-level evaluation 本身。
661	本文的差异更窄：把 profile groups 当作 profiler 输出，在同一批 operations 上比较 flat、fixed-session drilldown、dataset-native、raw-action 和 operation-stack views，并用 AP、nDCG、inspection budget recall、work-to-first-positive、fragmentation 和 profile-configuration actionability 评分。
662	AgentRx/TELBench-style traces 是后续 oracle/baseline 候选，不是当前已完成的 broader span-localization 证据。
663	
664	\textbf{Computer-use 和 tool-use benchmarks.}
665	WebLINX、Mind2Web、GUI-Odyssey、OSWorld/OSWorld-Human、OpenCUA/AgentNet、SATraj-OS、AgentRewardBench、ToolBench 和 tau-bench 为本文提供真实标注轨迹~[3--10,19--22]。
666	本文不提出新 benchmark。
667	贡献是把这些 benchmark 的动作、质量、安全和人工 group 标签统一为 operation fields，并用同一个 profiler 机制比较它们适合回答哪些 profiling 问题。
668	这些 benchmark 是 evidence source 和 native-sequence baseline，不是被本文替代的对象。
669	
670	\textbf{Novelty 边界。}
671	因此本文的新意不是“第一个 agent observability 系统”、不是“第一个 agent trajectory benchmark”、也不是“第一个 folded-stack 可视化”。
672	当前可 defend 的 scoped novelty 是：只用 operation 和 operation stack 两个 profiler 抽象，把 trace/session/span 作为输入容器或 baseline，在真实公开标注轨迹上把 profile groups 当成 ranking/localization outputs，并用 hidden labels 计算 accuracy、work、fragmentation 和 actionability。
673	更具体地说，新意不是 query-time aggregation 本身，而是把 agent-operation record、recursive multi-field stack shape 和 hidden-label localization benchmark 绑在一起：同一批 agent operations 因 stack shape 不同形成不同的可定位、可排序、可检查 aggregation units。
674	这不是穷尽式 2026 全量综述；它只界定当前 claim 的最近同问题威胁和已评估边界。
675	
676	\section{局限}
677	
678		当前证据支持的是 scoped profiling claim，而不是不加限定的 agent-analysis claim。
679		本节界定哪些结论可以写进主 claim，哪些只能作为 future work 或扩展实验。
680		第一，field derivation 和 boundary recovery 的范围仍然有限。
681		当前证据支持 deterministic mappings、label-derived rules 和部分 supervised boundary backends 能派生 stackable operation fields，但不证明无监督或 LLM-backed intent detector 已经解决，也不证明一个 backend 能跨所有标签家族工作。
682			AgentRewardBench looping 被简单 \texttt{repeat\_signal\_change} baseline 完全解释，这说明每个 family 都需要 suitability、calibration 和 simple-baseline 检查。
683	
684		第二，E2 支持 profiler-localization claim，但不支持人类效用 claim。
685		E2 把 failure、safety、quality 和 human-boundary 问题转成 hidden-label ranking/localization benchmark，并证明 operation-stack profiling 相对 flat summary 和 fixed-session drilldown 有 accuracy/work/fragmentation tradeoff。
686		这个 tradeoff 是 task- 和 metric-specific 的：最佳 visible view 不由单一 hierarchy 垄断，source-task selector 不能稳定自动选中最优 view，20\%/30\% inspection budget 下 operation-stack query-aware 的 median recall 更高，但 fixed-session 仍保留 first-positive 低成本反例。
687		Fixed-session fragmentation 与 operation-work 成本也必须分开解释：operation-stack 支持更少 group fragmentation 和同预算更少 groups，但 first-positive/work 指标仍不由 operation-stack 支配。
688		Related-work comparison 只把 closest-system grounding 转成 baseline threat，不增加新的实证结果。
689		我们已经把 6 个 tasks、3 个 views、24 个 participant slots 和 144 个 trials 整理成 balanced analyst-study protocol，并让 study materials 与 hidden answer key 分离。
690		但该 protocol 现在只是可选增强，用来验证开发者或 agent analyst 是否更快或更准。
691		本文当前不能推出开发者准确率、time-to-answer 或 productivity 改善，也不能声称所有 intent boundary 都能被自动发现。
692		论文主 claim 应固定为 profiler 本身在真实标注 trace 上的定位、排序、归因和 actionability，而不是 human utility。
693	
694		第三，数据和互操作范围是轻量采样。
695		本文避免同步完整测试集、图片归档和 gated 数据，因此有些来源只覆盖前缀、子配置或 redacted rows。
696		Chrome Trace Event 和 agent-session exchange 当前只提供 exchange/reproducibility evidence，覆盖本地 session fixture 和真实标注 operation 前缀。
697		这说明 trace 可以作为 exchange container，但不证明完整 OpenTelemetry/Chrome trace-ecosystem、Perfetto producer 或图像密集 benchmark 兼容。
698	
699			第四，E4 是复现和范围控制结果，不是额外的 profiler accuracy 结果。
700			Replay、数字对齐、数据来源选择和两个抽象的表述约束让正文没有越过已有实证结果。
701			如果采样或 oracle 本身有偏差，E4 能暴露不一致并迫使 claim 收窄，但不能消除偏差。
702			因此本文最终主张应固定为 two-abstraction mechanism 和 hidden-label profiler fidelity/work tradeoff，而不是 universal fixed-session dominance、automatic anomaly detection 或完整 human utility。
703	
704	\section{结论}
705	
706		本文把 agent semantic profiling 收敛为两个核心抽象：operation 和 operation stack。
707		Prompt、session、toolcall、process、syscall、plan、subagent、GUI action、安全标签和质量标签都只是 operation shapes 或 fields。
708		字段派生、查询过滤、权重选择、递归折叠和复现配置都围绕这两个抽象工作；profile spec 只是固定这些选择，deterministic output 只是让同一 profile 可以 byte-stable replay。
709		在 15 个轻量采样的公开标注轨迹数据源上，这个模型统一了 web、mobile、desktop、software、API、dialogue、failure、安全、human group 和 step-quality 轨迹，并产生 flamegraph 之外的 stack tree、transition、quality、boundary、case views 和 scope reports。
710		这支持本文的核心机制 claim：agent profiling 的边界可以从 prompt/session/span tree 中释放出来，成为 query-time operation-stack projection。
711	
712		当前最强经验结论来自四类 oracle-rich 轨迹。
713		OSWorld-Human 证明同一动作序列可以折叠到人工 grouped-action 深度；AgentNet 证明 step correctness 和 redundancy 可以作为普通 operation fields 进入 profiling；AgentRewardBench 和 SATraj-OS 证明 failure、looping、side-effect、安全和 attack-type diagnostics 可以用同一机制表达。
714		6 个 label-hidden tasks 构成主 hidden-label profiler benchmark：query-aware operation-stack top-5 groups 用 median 0.0937 work 取得 0.188 recall，flat summary 用 1.0 work 才取得 full recall，fixed-session 用 0.0163 work 但 top-5 recall 只有 0.0233；相对 fixed-session，operation-stack top-5 recall 在 5/6 tasks 上更高，并把 median groups 从 285.0 降到 157.5。
715	
716			补充分析把这个 profiler claim 的适用条件讲清楚。
717			Task-paired uncertainty、label-permutation negative controls、view/depth task-fit、inspection-budget curves、fixed-recall target、sequence-scope scoring 和 oracle-depth scoring 共同说明：operation-stack 的主要优势是 AP/work/fragmentation tradeoff，而不是所有指标支配。
718			Actionability 证据进一步显示 36/36 objective rows 有具体 optimization action，27/36 best visible policies 不是默认 operation-stack query-aware。
719			Diagnostic lenses、case views、baseline contrasts、action counterfactuals 和 held-out transfer results 说明 profiler 暴露的是可调分析 surface，而不是 automatic universal selector。
720		Executable profile-spec patch 进一步证明这种 profile-configuration actionability 可以落到 Rust profiler 配置上：5/6 patches 改善 AP、top-5 lift 和 first-positive work；OSWorld-Human reject 再由 boundary-derived operation fields 改善 AP 和 groups，但保留 work 反例。
721	
722		因此本文的新意不在单个 flamegraph，而在把 agent 轨迹先统一成 operations，再把边界选择推迟到 operation-stack 查询。
723		这个接口与 pprof、Perfetto、OpenTelemetry/OpenInference 和 LLM observability systems 互补，因为它不重新定义通用 trace schema，也不把 dashboard 当作贡献。
724		所有扩展都先写回 operation fields，再由同一 operation-stack query 折叠，包括 mapping/tagging、profile spec、agent-session trace、Chrome/Perfetto-style trace exchange 和 boundary-derived fields。
725		这样的限制让同一批 operations 可以按不同问题选择 view、派生字段和折叠深度，也让读者看到每个数字对应哪一类证据。
726		当前可写入论文的价值主张只覆盖相对 dataset-provided hidden labels 的 profiler fidelity、label-scored ranking/localization、inspection-cost/fragmentation tradeoff 和 profile-configuration actionability。
727		它不覆盖 detector、human utility、baseline dominance、automatic patch selector 或 ecosystem compatibility。
728		后续增强不应该无差别增加数据集。
729		更有价值的方向有两个。
730		第一，field-derivation backend 需要跨家族 calibration，并稳定胜过简单 sequence-derived baselines。
731		第二，我们需要在已有或新增真实 trace 中补更强的 instruction-step、solution-path 或 human subtask oracle。
732		只有当论文要提出 ecosystem-baseline 主张时，才应该导入真实 OTel/Phoenix/LangSmith/Langfuse/Perfetto span-tree trace。
733		Controlled human 或 agent analyst study 可以作为后续增强，但不是本文主 profiling claim 的前置条件。

主要指标包括 spec pass rate、profiler invocation 数量、median/p95 runtime、sample equality、stack equality、raw-byte output equality 和 input-source coverage。
这个问题只覆盖离线路径复现，不覆盖 live eBPF overhead、human utility、complete ecosystem compatibility 或 automatic universal selection。

本节的 empirical content 是一个 replayability/cost result。
在同一批 operation JSONL inputs 上，\toolname{} 重复执行 76 个 profile specs，共 152 次 profiler invocations。
默认模式下所有 specs 在重复运行中保持 semantic profile content、samples 和 unique stacks 稳定，median 每个 spec 运行时间为 1.581s，p95 为 2.719s；raw-byte determinism 只有 4/76，因为输出带生成时间戳。
Deterministic replay mode 固定 JSON \texttt{generated\_at} 和 pprof profile time 后，同一 76 个 specs 的 semantic 与 raw-byte determinism 均为 76/76，median 每个 spec 运行时间为 1.601s，p95 为 2.767s。
这些结果说明复现者可以重放离线 profile content，并在需要时得到 byte-stable profile files。
它们不等价于 live capture overhead，也不形成另一个经验性 profiling 实验。

输入来源 replay 说明 profile spec 是真正的数据入口配置，而不是只包了一层 output path。
Rust profile-spec path 现在可以携带 \texttt{session\_files}、\texttt{trace\_files}、\texttt{standard\_trace\_files}、regex \texttt{tag\_rules}、predicates、rank rules、stack overrides 和 \texttt{include\_standard\_trace\_args}。
回归测试把同一个 public Codex fixture 作为 local session 和 exported agent-session trace replay，并把一个 generic Chrome Trace Event 中的非 AgentSight \texttt{protocol} arg 导入为 operation field 后折叠。
这些输入在导入后都归一成普通 operations，再由同一 operation-stack machinery 折叠。
这个结果支持 trace exchange 的最低复现要求，但不支持完整 trace-ecosystem compatibility claim。
表~\ref{tab:e4-replay-cost} 和表~\ref{tab:e4-determinism} 是 E4 的两个主显示。
前者呈现 replayability/cost result，后者呈现 deterministic-output repair。
表中的 labels 只标识 profile-spec families，不是新的 accuracy 实验。

除了两张主表，RQ4 还约束论文数字、数据来源选择和明确排除的主张。
这些一致性约束只核对已经报告的 profile results 和当前论文文本，不重新排名、不下载、不同步、不创建、不重标数据集、不重跑 profiler，也不运行 human/agent analyst task。
上一节的 actionability 结论依赖这些可复现 profile specs 和 operation inputs；本节不重新验证 fidelity/accuracy、actionability 或 baseline tradeoff，只证明复现者能重放这些 specs，并核对正文数字、数据来源选择和主张边界。
因此 RQ4/E4 是 replayability/scope evidence，不是人工 analyst 主观解释、live overhead 或新的 profiler accuracy 结果。

E4 的辅助材料只约束正文和可重放结果的一致性。
它们把论文主张、数据来源选择、明确排除的结论和 operation/operation-stack 边界对齐到 replayed profiles。
这些材料帮助读者判断论文是否把证据写过头，但不增加 localization、actionability 或 overhead claim。
这些辅助视图可以支持 E1--E4，但不会形成额外主实验。

\section{数据源选择与扩展边界}

当前数据选择遵循 oracle-first 原则。
Operation-stack profiling 的主 claim 需要有顺序、有动作、并且能隐藏评分标签的真实轨迹。
规模更大的数据集如果缺少这些字段，只能支撑覆盖范围，不能支撑 localization accuracy。
OSWorld-Human 提供 single-action 和 grouped-action，因此最直接支撑递归边界验证。
AgentNet 同时提供大规模人工桌面任务和 per-step correctness/redundancy，因此支撑 step-quality profiling。
AgentRewardBench 和 SATraj-OS 把评估目标从 action taxonomy 推到 failure、looping、安全和 side-effect diagnostics。
GUI-Odyssey、tau-bench 和 ToolBench 则作为跨域覆盖来源，说明 operation abstraction 可以覆盖移动 GUI、user-agent-tool dialogue 和 API/tool traces，而不局限于桌面轨迹。

ScaleCUA 的作用是扩大 GUI history 覆盖，而不是提供新的主证据。
我们使用的 ScaleCUA stream sample 含 5,000 个 Ubuntu navigation rows，覆盖 131 个 sessions，最大 step 为 48。
该子集的 action taxonomy 主要是 click 和 terminate，所以 phase/action 指标达到 1.0 并不表示强泛化。
它更适合证明 multi-step GUI history context 可以被投影为 \texttt{history\_state} 和 \texttt{history\_depth} fields，而不是证明复杂边界 detector。

\section{相关工作}

\textbf{Profiling、flamegraphs 和 trace analysis.}
传统 flamegraph 和 pprof 路线把运行时调用栈折叠成热点视图~[1,16,17]。
pprof 不只是固定 call stack：它支持 sample tags，也支持用 \texttt{tagroot}/\texttt{tagleaf} 把 tag value 作为 pseudo stack frame 可视化~[17]。
Perfetto 则代表系统 trace ingestion、SQL trace analysis、trace summary 和 derived events 的成熟方向~[18]。
因此本文不能把 novelty 写成“只有我们支持 query-time aggregation”。
本文复用 folded-stack 表示，但 scoped novelty 是 agent-operation record model、recursive multi-field operation-stack projection 和真实标注轨迹上的 hidden-label localization benchmark 这三者的组合。
Stack frame 来自 agent operation fields，而不是语言运行时函数调用或通用 trace SQL schema。
因此同一批 operations 可以被折叠为 task、phase、tool、action、quality 或 safety 视图，也可以改成 fixed-session 或 flat baseline。
区别不在图形样式，而在 agent 语义对象、递归多字段 stack projection 和跨数据集 hidden-label scoring。

\textbf{Agent tracing 和 LLM observability.}
OpenTelemetry GenAI 和 OpenInference 标准化 GenAI spans、LLM calls、agent reasoning steps、tool invocations、retrieval operations、MCP 和 provider-specific telemetry~[2,11]。
LangSmith、Langfuse、Phoenix 和 AgentOps 等系统进一步把 LLM call、tool call、latency、token、trace tree、session、observation、evaluation score、goal、plan 和 agent artifact 放进单次 workflow inspection 与生产监控~[12,13,14,15]。
这些系统是本文最接近的同问题相关工作。
因此本文把 trace/span/session 明确当作 exchange container 或 baseline shape，而不是加成第三个 profiler 抽象。
E2 实际评估的是 fixed-session drilldown 这个 trace-tree-shaped baseline；真实 OpenTelemetry/OpenInference/Phoenix span-tree import 仍是后续互操作 baseline，不是当前已完成结果。
本文关注跨轨迹 semantic profiling，把异构标注轨迹或本地 agent 历史统一为 operations，并允许用户选择 stack 深度、mappings、tagging 和 ranker。
因此本文把这些系统作为同问题 baseline threat，而不是声称替代现有 observability products。

\textbf{Agent failure 和 span localization。}
2026 年的 AgentRx、TELBench/DRIFT、Holistic Evaluation and Failure Diagnosis 和 AgentAtlas 是最接近的同问题威胁~[23--26]。
AgentRx 发布带 critical failure step 和 failure category 的失败轨迹，并用 constraint checking 与 LLM judge 做 root-cause localization。
TELBench/DRIFT 把 deep-research agent 轨迹转成 semantic spans，并标注 harmful error spans。
Holistic Diagnosis 把 agent-level diagnosis 和 span-level evaluation 结合起来；AgentAtlas 则强调 outcome leaderboard 不能覆盖 trajectory quality 和 control-decision quality。
因此本文不能把 novelty 写成 failure localization、trajectory diagnosis 或 span-level evaluation 本身。
本文的差异更窄：把 profile groups 当作 profiler 输出，在同一批 operations 上比较 flat、fixed-session drilldown、dataset-native、raw-action 和 operation-stack views，并用 AP、nDCG、inspection budget recall、work-to-first-positive、fragmentation 和 profile-configuration actionability 评分。
AgentRx/TELBench-style traces 是后续 oracle/baseline 候选，不是当前已完成的 broader span-localization 证据。

\textbf{Computer-use 和 tool-use benchmarks.}
WebLINX、Mind2Web、GUI-Odyssey、OSWorld/OSWorld-Human、OpenCUA/AgentNet、SATraj-OS、AgentRewardBench、ToolBench 和 tau-bench 为本文提供真实标注轨迹~[3--10,19--22]。
本文不提出新 benchmark。
贡献是把这些 benchmark 的动作、质量、安全和人工 group 标签统一为 operation fields，并用同一个 profiler 机制比较它们适合回答哪些 profiling 问题。
这些 benchmark 是 evidence source 和 native-sequence baseline，不是被本文替代的对象。

\textbf{Novelty 边界。}
因此本文的新意不是“第一个 agent observability 系统”、不是“第一个 agent trajectory benchmark”、也不是“第一个 folded-stack 可视化”。
当前可 defend 的 scoped novelty 是：只用 operation 和 operation stack 两个 profiler 抽象，把 trace/session/span 作为输入容器或 baseline，在真实公开标注轨迹上把 profile groups 当成 ranking/localization outputs，并用 hidden labels 计算 accuracy、work、fragmentation 和 actionability。
更具体地说，新意不是 query-time aggregation 本身，而是把 agent-operation record、recursive multi-field stack shape 和 hidden-label localization benchmark 绑在一起：同一批 agent operations 因 stack shape 不同形成不同的可定位、可排序、可检查 aggregation units。
这不是穷尽式 2026 全量综述；它只界定当前 claim 的最近同问题威胁和已评估边界。

\section{局限}

	当前证据支持的是 scoped profiling claim，而不是不加限定的 agent-analysis claim。
	本节界定哪些结论可以写进主 claim，哪些只能作为 future work 或扩展实验。
	第一，field derivation 和 boundary recovery 的范围仍然有限。
	当前证据支持 deterministic mappings、label-derived rules 和部分 supervised boundary backends 能派生 stackable operation fields，但不证明无监督或 LLM-backed intent detector 已经解决，也不证明一个 backend 能跨所有标签家族工作。
		AgentRewardBench looping 被简单 \texttt{repeat\_signal\_change} baseline 完全解释，这说明每个 family 都需要 suitability、calibration 和 simple-baseline 检查。

	第二，E2 支持 profiler-localization claim，但不支持人类效用 claim。
	E2 把 failure、safety、quality 和 human-boundary 问题转成 hidden-label ranking/localization benchmark，并证明 operation-stack profiling 相对 flat summary 和 fixed-session drilldown 有 accuracy/work/fragmentation tradeoff。
	这个 tradeoff 是 task- 和 metric-specific 的：最佳 visible view 不由单一 hierarchy 垄断，source-task selector 不能稳定自动选中最优 view，20\%/30\% inspection budget 下 operation-stack query-aware 的 median recall 更高，但 fixed-session 仍保留 first-positive 低成本反例。
	Fixed-session fragmentation 与 operation-work 成本也必须分开解释：operation-stack 支持更少 group fragmentation 和同预算更少 groups，但 first-positive/work 指标仍不由 operation-stack 支配。
	Related-work comparison 只把 closest-system grounding 转成 baseline threat，不增加新的实证结果。
	我们已经把 6 个 tasks、3 个 views、24 个 participant slots 和 144 个 trials 整理成 balanced analyst-study protocol，并让 study materials 与 hidden answer key 分离。
	但该 protocol 现在只是可选增强，用来验证开发者或 agent analyst 是否更快或更准。
	本文当前不能推出开发者准确率、time-to-answer 或 productivity 改善，也不能声称所有 intent boundary 都能被自动发现。
	论文主 claim 应固定为 profiler 本身在真实标注 trace 上的定位、排序、归因和 actionability，而不是 human utility。

	第三，数据和互操作范围是轻量采样。
	本文避免同步完整测试集、图片归档和 gated 数据，因此有些来源只覆盖前缀、子配置或 redacted rows。
	Chrome Trace Event 和 agent-session exchange 当前只提供 exchange/reproducibility evidence，覆盖本地 session fixture 和真实标注 operation 前缀。
	这说明 trace 可以作为 exchange container，但不证明完整 OpenTelemetry/Chrome trace-ecosystem、Perfetto producer 或图像密集 benchmark 兼容。

		第四，E4 是复现和范围控制结果，不是额外的 profiler accuracy 结果。
		Replay、数字对齐、数据来源选择和两个抽象的表述约束让正文没有越过已有实证结果。
		如果采样或 oracle 本身有偏差，E4 能暴露不一致并迫使 claim 收窄，但不能消除偏差。
		因此本文最终主张应固定为 two-abstraction mechanism 和 hidden-label profiler fidelity/work tradeoff，而不是 universal fixed-session dominance、automatic anomaly detection 或完整 human utility。

\section{结论}

	本文把 agent semantic profiling 收敛为两个核心抽象：operation 和 operation stack。
	Prompt、session、toolcall、process、syscall、plan、subagent、GUI action、安全标签和质量标签都只是 operation shapes 或 fields。
	字段派生、查询过滤、权重选择、递归折叠和复现配置都围绕这两个抽象工作；profile spec 只是固定这些选择，deterministic output 只是让同一 profile 可以 byte-stable replay。
	在 15 个轻量采样的公开标注轨迹数据源上，这个模型统一了 web、mobile、desktop、software、API、dialogue、failure、安全、human group 和 step-quality 轨迹，并产生 flamegraph 之外的 stack tree、transition、quality、boundary、case views 和 scope reports。
	这支持本文的核心机制 claim：agent profiling 的边界可以从 prompt/session/span tree 中释放出来，成为 query-time operation-stack projection。

	当前最强经验结论来自四类 oracle-rich 轨迹。
	OSWorld-Human 证明同一动作序列可以折叠到人工 grouped-action 深度；AgentNet 证明 step correctness 和 redundancy 可以作为普通 operation fields 进入 profiling；AgentRewardBench 和 SATraj-OS 证明 failure、looping、side-effect、安全和 attack-type diagnostics 可以用同一机制表达。
	6 个 label-hidden tasks 构成主 hidden-label profiler benchmark：query-aware operation-stack top-5 groups 用 median 0.0937 work 取得 0.188 recall，flat summary 用 1.0 work 才取得 full recall，fixed-session 用 0.0163 work 但 top-5 recall 只有 0.0233；相对 fixed-session，operation-stack top-5 recall 在 5/6 tasks 上更高，并把 median groups 从 285.0 降到 157.5。

		补充分析把这个 profiler claim 的适用条件讲清楚。
		Task-paired uncertainty、label-permutation negative controls、view/depth task-fit、inspection-budget curves、fixed-recall target、sequence-scope scoring 和 oracle-depth scoring 共同说明：operation-stack 的主要优势是 AP/work/fragmentation tradeoff，而不是所有指标支配。
		Actionability 证据进一步显示 36/36 objective rows 有具体 optimization action，27/36 best visible policies 不是默认 operation-stack query-aware。
		Diagnostic lenses、case views、baseline contrasts、action counterfactuals 和 held-out transfer results 说明 profiler 暴露的是可调分析 surface，而不是 automatic universal selector。
	Executable profile-spec patch 进一步证明这种 profile-configuration actionability 可以落到 Rust profiler 配置上：5/6 patches 改善 AP、top-5 lift 和 first-positive work；OSWorld-Human reject 再由 boundary-derived operation fields 改善 AP 和 groups，但保留 work 反例。

	因此本文的新意不在单个 flamegraph，而在把 agent 轨迹先统一成 operations，再把边界选择推迟到 operation-stack 查询。
	这个接口与 pprof、Perfetto、OpenTelemetry/OpenInference 和 LLM observability systems 互补，因为它不重新定义通用 trace schema，也不把 dashboard 当作贡献。
	所有扩展都先写回 operation fields，再由同一 operation-stack query 折叠，包括 mapping/tagging、profile spec、agent-session trace、Chrome/Perfetto-style trace exchange 和 boundary-derived fields。
	这样的限制让同一批 operations 可以按不同问题选择 view、派生字段和折叠深度，也让读者看到每个数字对应哪一类证据。
	当前可写入论文的价值主张只覆盖相对 dataset-provided hidden labels 的 profiler fidelity、label-scored ranking/localization、inspection-cost/fragmentation tradeoff 和 profile-configuration actionability。
	它不覆盖 detector、human utility、baseline dominance、automatic patch selector 或 ecosystem compatibility。
	后续增强不应该无差别增加数据集。
	更有价值的方向有两个。
	第一，field-derivation backend 需要跨家族 calibration，并稳定胜过简单 sequence-derived baselines。
	第二，我们需要在已有或新增真实 trace 中补更强的 instruction-step、solution-path 或 human subtask oracle。
	只有当论文要提出 ecosystem-baseline 主张时，才应该导入真实 OTel/Phoenix/LangSmith/Langfuse/Perfetto span-tree trace。
	Controlled human 或 agent analyst study 可以作为后续增强，但不是本文主 profiling claim 的前置条件。

1	\documentclass[sigconf]{acmart}
2	
3	\setcopyright{none}
4	\settopmatter{printacmref=false}
5	\renewcommand\footnotetextcopyrightpermission[1]{}
6	\pagestyle{plain}

12	\usepackage{graphicx}

15	\newcommand{\operation}{\texttt{operation}\xspace}
16	\newcommand{\opstack}{\texttt{operation stack}\xspace}
17	
18	\begin{document}
19	
20	\title{AgentPProf: Semantic Profiling for AI Agent Traces}
21	
22	\begin{abstract}
23	AI agents produce complex execution traces spanning prompts, LLM calls,
24	tool invocations, GUI actions, and system effects. As deployments grow
25	to hundreds of sessions, both human operators and automated analysis
26	pipelines need aggregate views, not just per-execution debugging.
27	Existing observability tools organize events into fixed session/span
28	hierarchies suited for single-run debugging but unable to fold events
29	across sessions by semantic work category.
30	We show that agent profiling reduces to two abstractions once intent
31	recognition restores the deterministic-label precondition that
32	flame-graph folding requires.
33	An \emph{operation} is a uniform weighted record for any agent activity.
34	An \emph{operation stack} is a field projection chosen at query time.
35	\toolname implements this model with pluggable intent-recognition
36	backends (regex rules, local LLM tagging, unsupervised clustering) and
37	produces flame graphs, pprof profiles, and structured JSON consumable by
38	both developers and analysis agents.
39	On 325 real agent sessions, semantic labels separate 90\% of
40	system-effect weight that flat views merge. On six localization tasks across four public datasets
41	(34{,}539 operations), operation-stack profiling reduces inspection work
42	by 90\% versus flat summaries and group fragmentation by 45\% versus
43	fixed-session drilldown. On 7/9 held-out datasets, leave-dataset-out mapping achieves V-measure
44	above 0.7.
45	\end{abstract}
46	
47	\maketitle
48	
49	%% ===================================================================
50	\section{Introduction}
51	\label{sec:intro}
52	
53	%% ¶1: Background + Context
54	AI agent systems produce heterogeneous execution traces spanning
55	prompts, LLM calls, tool invocations, GUI actions, and system effects.
56	As deployments scale to hundreds of sessions and tens of thousands of
57	calls, both developers and automated analysis agents need aggregate
58	views, including which categories of work consume the most tokens, where
59	failures concentrate, and how cost distributes across semantic task
60	families.
61	
62	%% ¶2: Problem + example
63	However, no existing observability tool folds events across sessions
64	into an aggregate cost distribution. LangSmith~\cite{langsmith},
65	Langfuse~\cite{langfuse}, Phoenix~\cite{phoenix}, and OpenTelemetry
66	GenAI~\cite{otel} organize events into per-execution timelines and
67	span trees, enabling single-run debugging but not cross-session
68	aggregation. In a real development project, the system effect
69	\texttt{process:cargo; effect:test; status:ok} appears 2{,}903 times
70	across 325 sessions, yet no existing trace tool can disaggregate these
71	executions by the semantic intent that triggered them.
72	
73	%% ¶3: Root cause
74	CPU profilers solved the equivalent aggregation problem for programs.
75	Flame graphs~\cite{flamegraphs} fold millions of function-call samples
76	into a single chart where width represents cost. The key enabler is
77	\emph{deterministic} function names that merge identical call stacks.
78	Agent traces break this precondition because prompts are natural
79	language, and
80	two prompts expressing the same intent share no characters
81	(\S\ref{sec:background}).
82	
83	%% ¶4: Existing solutions fail
84	Some existing tools take steps toward semantic grouping. Datadog LLM
85	Observability clusters user messages by
86	topic,\footnote{\url{https://docs.datadoghq.com/llm_observability/}}
87	and Laminar extracts structured signals from
88	traces.\footnote{\url{https://docs.lmnr.ai/signals/introduction}} Both characterize \emph{input distributions} (``30\% of users ask code
89	questions'') but not \emph{resource attribution} (``code-review tasks
90	consume 40\% of the token budget'').
91	
92	%% ¶5: Key insight
93	We observe that agent observability requires \emph{semantic profiling},
94	meaning aggregate, cross-session cost attribution grouped by user
95	intent, as distinct from execution-structural groupings like sessions or
96	spans. The obstacle is the nondeterminism of natural-language identifiers.
97	Intent recognition can restore deterministic labels, making semantic
98	profiling tractable.
99	
100	%% ¶6: This paper + numbers
101	This paper presents \toolname, a profiler that restores aggregate
102	flame-graph analysis for agent traces. The profiler is built on two
103	abstractions: an \emph{operation} (a uniform weighted record for any
104	agent activity) and an \emph{operation stack} (a field projection chosen
105	at query time). \toolname recovers the deterministic-label precondition through
106	\emph{intent recognition}, which maps free-form prompts to stable labels
107	using pluggable backends (regex rules, local LLM tagging, or
108	unsupervised clustering). On 325 real sessions, semantic labels separate
109	90\% of system-effect weight that flat views merge. On four public
110	datasets,
111	operation-stack profiling reduces inspection work by 90\% versus flat
112	summaries.
113	
114	%% ¶7: Contributions
115	This paper makes three contributions:
116	
117	\begin{enumerate}
118	\item \textbf{Insight: agent profiling reduces to two abstractions.}
119	  We show that fixed session/span hierarchies cannot fold by semantic
120	  category, and that combining uniform operation records with query-time
121	  stack projections closes this aggregation gap once intent recognition
122	  restores deterministic labels
123	  (\S\ref{sec:background}--\S\ref{sec:design}).
124	\item \textbf{System: \toolname.}
125	  We implement this model as a Rust CLI with pluggable intent
126	  recognition, four built-in views, and output formats (pprof, SVG,
127	  JSON) consumable by both developers and automated analysis agents
128	  (\S\ref{sec:impl}).
129	\item \textbf{Evaluation.}
130	  We show that semantic labels separate 90\% of system-effect weight
131	  that unsemantic views merge (RQ1), that operation-stack profiling
132	  localizes hidden labeled problems with 90\% less work than flat
133	  summaries (RQ2), and that mapping-derived labels agree with
134	  ground-truth annotations on 7/9 public datasets (RQ3)
135	  (\S\ref{sec:eval}).
136	\end{enumerate}
137	
138	%% ===================================================================
139	\section{Background and Motivation}
140	\label{sec:background}
141	
142	\subsection{How Existing Agent Trace Models Work}
143	
144	Current agent observability tools organize traces around fixed
145	hierarchies. OpenTelemetry represents an execution as a \emph{trace}
146	containing a tree of \emph{spans}, each with a name, duration, and
147	key-value attributes. LangSmith and Langfuse group spans into
148	\emph{sessions} and display them as timelines or waterfall charts.
149	Phoenix and OpenInference add GenAI-specific span types for LLM calls,
150	tool invocations, retrieval steps, and agent reasoning.
151	
152	These models share a structural property, namely that the session or
153	span tree is the skeleton of the data. Every event belongs to exactly one span, and
154	spans nest in a fixed parent-child hierarchy determined at execution
155	time. This design is effective for debugging because a developer can
156	locate a failing span, inspect its attributes, and trace its parent
157	chain to understand the execution context.
158	
159	\subsection{Why Fixed Hierarchies Cannot Profile}
160	
161	Profiling requires a fundamentally different operation, \emph{folding}
162	events across executions by semantic category so that width represents
163	aggregate cost. Fixed session/span hierarchies obstruct this in three
164	ways.
165	
166	First, sessions are boundaries, not categories. A single session may
167	contain review, debugging, and refactoring phases, and splitting by
168	session assigns all of them to the same bucket. Conversely, two sessions
169	performing the same task produce separate buckets that cannot be merged
170	without external logic. Second, span names describe mechanisms
171	(\texttt{LLMCall}, \texttt{ToolInvoke}, \texttt{ChatCompletion}), not
172	user intent (\texttt{review}, \texttt{debug}, \texttt{test}). Grouping
173	by span name tells you how many LLM calls occurred, not which categories
174	of work consumed the budget. Third, these limitations compound in practice. A common system effect
175	like running a test suite may appear thousands of times across sessions,
176	but a flat process summary shows only a single counter with no way to
177	attribute executions to the semantic intent that triggered them. We
178	quantify this disaggregation in RQ1~(\S\ref{sec:eval}).
179	
180	\subsection{Why CPU Profiling Does Not Directly Apply}
181	
182	CPU profilers solve the equivalent aggregation problem for programs.
183	A flame graph~\cite{flamegraphs} represents a profile as a set of
184	weighted \emph{samples}, each attached to a \emph{call stack} (an
185	ordered list of function frames). Identical stacks merge, and width
186	represents aggregate cost. The key enabler is that function names are
187	\emph{deterministic}. The same code path always produces the same
188	frames.
189	
190	Agent traces break this precondition. Prompts are natural language and
191	lack deterministic identifiers. Tool calls, GUI
192	actions, and process events are named heterogeneously across agent
193	families. Raw event names cannot serve as flame-graph frames.
194	
195	These observations yield three design requirements:
196	
197	\begin{description}
198	\item[R1: Uniform record type.]
199	  Agent traces mix prompts, LLM calls, tool invocations, GUI actions,
200	  process events, and benchmark labels. The profiler needs a single
201	  record type that can represent all of them without type-specific
202	  objects.
203	\item[R2: Query-time aggregation.]
204	  The same data must support multiple aggregation shapes (by task,
205	  phase, action, session, or dataset) without rebuilding the trace.
206	  Sessions and spans must be fields, not fixed hierarchy nodes.
207	\item[R3: Deterministic labels for folding.]
208	  Free-form prompts must be mapped to short, stable, repeatable labels
209	  before folding. This \emph{intent recognition} step has no analogue in
210	  CPU profiling, where function names are already deterministic.
211	\end{description}
212	
213	%% ===================================================================
214	\section{Design}
215	\label{sec:design}
216	
217	The three requirements (a uniform record type, query-time aggregation,
218	and deterministic labels for folding) drive the design. We introduce two
219	abstractions that satisfy R1 and R2, operations (\S\ref{sec:ops}) and
220	operation stacks (\S\ref{sec:stacks}), and a pluggable
221	intent-recognition mechanism (\S\ref{sec:intent}) that satisfies R3.
222	
223	\subsection{Operations (R1: Uniform Record Type)}
224	\label{sec:ops}
225	
226	A profiler should not distinguish between prompts, tool calls, and
227	process events at the object-model level. \toolname uses a single
228	abstraction. An \operation is a weighted record with string fields and
229	additive measures.
230	
231	Each operation carries string fields (\texttt{project}, \texttt{agent},
232	\texttt{session}, \texttt{prompt\_tag}, \texttt{kind}, \texttt{model},
233	\texttt{path}, \texttt{domain}, \texttt{status}, \ldots) and additive
234	measures (token count, duration, occurrence count). A prompt, an LLM
235	call, a tool invocation, a file read, a GUI click, and a process event
236	are all operation records that differ only in which fields are populated.
237	
238	\subsection{Operation Stacks (R2: Query-Time Aggregation)}
239	\label{sec:stacks}
240	
241	An \opstack is an ordered list of fields chosen at query time. Folding
242	operations by that list produces the standard folded-stack
243	representation:
244	
245	\begin{small}
246	\begin{verbatim}
247	CPU:   main;parse;tokenize          42
248	Agent: prompt:debug;call:llm;tool:bash  4200
249	\end{verbatim}
250	\end{small}
251	
252	\noindent Unlike CPU profiling, where the call stack is determined by
253	execution, the operation stack is determined by the query. The same
254	operations can be folded as a flat task summary, a fixed-session tree, a
255	semantic phase/action hierarchy, or a dataset-native trajectory.
256	Changing the fields changes the aggregation without changing the data.
257	
258	Query-time stack selection directly addresses the fixed-hierarchy problem
259	from \S\ref{sec:background}. Sessions and spans are optional operation
260	fields,
261	not structural skeleton nodes. Including \texttt{session} in the stack
262	produces a per-session drilldown (equivalent to a trace tree). Excluding
263	it produces a cross-session aggregate (which no existing trace tool
264	provides). The same data supports both debugging and profiling views.
265	
266	A \emph{view} is a triple $(\varphi, \sigma, w)$. The predicate
267	$\varphi$ selects which operations participate, the stack function
268	$\sigma$ maps each operation to a frame sequence, and the weight
269	function $w$ assigns a nonnegative measure. The view formalism supports arbitrary user-defined
270	views. Four built-in defaults (Table~\ref{tab:views}) answer common
271	questions.
272	
273	\begin{table}[t]
274	\centering\small
275	\caption{Built-in views. Each shares the same operation set
276	but selects different activities, stack structures, and weights.}
277	\label{tab:views}
278	\begin{tabular}{llll}
279	\toprule
280	View & $\varphi$ (select) & $w$ (width) & Question \\
281	\midrule
282	\texttt{tokens} & LLM calls & token count & Budget distribution? \\
283	\texttt{time} & All timed ops & duration (s) & Time distribution? \\
284	\texttt{files} & File-effect ops & event count & Repo coverage? \\
285	\texttt{network} & Net-effect ops & event count & External contacts? \\
286	\bottomrule
287	\end{tabular}
288	\end{table}
289	
290	\begin{figure}[t]
291	\centering
292	% \includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/fig-architecture.pdf}
293	\fbox{\parbox{0.93\linewidth}{\centering\small
294	[Architecture: Agent trace files (Codex/Claude JSONL, benchmark JSONL)
295	$\to$ Parser / Importer $\to$ Intent Recognition (regex / LLM / clustering)
296	or Mapping Rules $\to$ Operations with fields $\to$ Stack query
297	$(\varphi, \sigma, w)$ $\to$ Folded stacks $\to$ Flame graph / pprof /
298	JSON]}}
299	\caption{System architecture. Local agent histories enter through
300	\texttt{agent-session} parsing. Public datasets enter as operation JSONL.
301	Both paths produce operations. The stack query and output are identical.}
302	\Description{Data flow from agent traces through parsing and intent
303	recognition to folded-stack flame graphs.}
304	\label{fig:architecture}
305	\end{figure}
306	
307	\subsection{Intent Recognition (R3: Deterministic Labels)}
308	\label{sec:intent}
309	
310	Operations and stacks handle heterogeneity and flexible aggregation, but
311	folding still requires deterministic frame labels, the precondition
312	that agent prompts violate (\S\ref{sec:background}). \toolname solves
313	this through \emph{intent recognition}, mapping free-form prompts to
314	short, stable labels before stack construction.
315	
316	The design uses a pluggable tagger framework with three backends:
317	
318	\paragraph{Regex rules with agent-assisted iteration.}
319	The production default. Rules have the form
320	\texttt{KIND:TAG=REGEX}, where \texttt{KIND} is \texttt{prompt},
321	\texttt{llm}, or \texttt{all}, \texttt{TAG} is a short lowercase label,
322	and \texttt{REGEX} is a pattern. Rules are evaluated in order; the first
323	match wins. The workflow is human--agent collaborative. The developer runs \toolname,
324	observes the unmatched rate and sample prompts, adds rules, re-runs, and
325	iterates until unmatched drops below 5\%. This typically takes 5--10
326	rounds. The resulting rule set is deterministic, reproducible, and
327	version-controllable.
328	
329	\paragraph{Local LLM tagger.}
330	For exploration or complex multilingual prompts, a local model
331	(e.g., a 3B-parameter GGUF via llama.cpp) generates a single-word label
332	per prompt. Grammar-constrained decoding ensures output validity.
333	Labels are cached, so re-runs with unchanged prompts incur zero LLM calls.
334	
335	\paragraph{Unsupervised clustering.}
336	TF-IDF vectorization followed by K-Means discovers natural prompt groups
337	without predefined rules, feeding rule authoring.
338	
339	The one-word label design is deliberate. Flame-graph frames must be
340	short because long summaries make charts unreadable. Labels serve navigation
341	and aggregation, not correctness verdicts.
342	
343	For structured traces such as public benchmark datasets, where action
344	types, tool names, and quality annotations are explicit fields, intent
345	recognition is unnecessary. \toolname supports
346	deterministic \emph{mapping rules} that derive new operation fields from
347	existing ones before stack construction. A \emph{profile spec} records
348	the complete analysis configuration (data sources, mappings, predicates,
349	stack fields, and outputs) for deterministic replay. This dual path
350	explains why \toolname handles both real agent sessions (which need
351	intent recognition) and public benchmark traces (which need mapping
352	rules). Both paths produce operations with fields, and the stack query
353	works identically on both.
354	
355	%% ===================================================================
356	\section{Implementation}
357	\label{sec:impl}
358	
359	\toolname is an offline, post-hoc profiler implemented as a Rust CLI
360	(Figure~\ref{fig:architecture}). It reads recorded traces, not live
361	events. The \texttt{agent-session} crate reads Codex and Claude Code local JSONL
362	history files and reconstructs prompts, LLM calls, tool invocations, and
363	their triggered file and network effects. Each prompt opens a span. LLM
364	calls, tool calls, and system effects within that span inherit its
365	semantic label, connecting intent to system behavior without runtime
366	instrumentation. Public benchmark datasets enter as operation JSONL with
367	mapping rules deriving fields before stack construction. Standard Chrome
368	Trace Event format can also be imported, with non-\toolname protocol
369	fields preserved as operation fields.
370	
371	Output formats include pprof protobuf (compatible with
372	\texttt{go tool pprof -http}), folded-stack text (compatible with
373	\texttt{flamegraph.pl}), standalone SVG flame graphs, and JSON summaries.
374	All outputs are deterministic given the same input and profile spec.
375	
376	\toolname is the offline profiling component of the AgentSight
377	observability framework. AgentSight provides real-time eBPF-based
378	capture of SSL traffic, process events, and file/network effects.
379	\toolname aggregates the recorded traces into semantic profiles. The two
380	are complementary. AgentSight answers ``what happened during this run''
381	(debugging), \toolname answers ``where did the budget go across runs''
382	(profiling).
383	
384	%% ===================================================================
385	\section{Evaluation}
386	\label{sec:eval}
387	
388	We organize the evaluation around three research questions.
389	
390	\paragraph{Evaluation setup.}
391	We use two classes of data. \emph{Real agent sessions}: 325 readable
392	local sessions (198~Codex, 50~Claude, 77~Claude subagent) from a
393	multi-month development project, containing 183{,}714 system
394	observations. \emph{Public labeled traces}: 15 families covering web,
395	mobile, desktop, software, API, and dialogue agents
396	(Table~\ref{tab:datasets}), totaling 47{,}590 operations through
397	mapping rules. All public traces are real agent or human executions
398	collected and labeled by their respective benchmark projects. Four
399	oracle-rich families (AgentRewardBench, SATraj-OS, AgentNet,
400	OSWorld-Human) provide hidden ground-truth labels for RQ2.
401

403	\centering\small

405	human executions. The bottom four rows provide oracle labels for RQ2.}

424	%% -------------------------------------------------------------------
425	\subsection{RQ1: Does Semantic Profiling Separate What Flat Views Mix?}
426	
427	The strongest argument against semantic profiling is that traditional
428	tools ``can already see the same information.'' RQ1 tests this claim
429	directly by measuring how much system-effect weight falls into
430	\emph{mixed-intent} buckets (those containing observations from
431	multiple semantic regions) under different projection choices.
432	
433	\begin{table}[t]
434	\centering\small
435	\caption{Semantic-axis ablation on 183{,}714 system observations
436	from 325 real sessions. All rows preserve the same total weight.}
437	\label{tab:mixing}
438	\begin{tabular}{lrrr}
439	\toprule
440	Projection & Unique stacks & Mixed wt.\% & Residual\% \\
441	\midrule
442	No semantic labels & 11{,}967 & 90.4 & 44.7 \\
443	Session label only & 15{,}027 & 84.4 & 33.4 \\
444	Prompt label only & 24{,}703 & 36.7 & 7.5 \\
445	Session + prompt & 26{,}829 & 0.0 & 0.0 \\
446	\bottomrule
447	\end{tabular}
448	\end{table}
449	
450	Table~\ref{tab:mixing} shows the result on 325 real Codex/Claude
451	sessions. Without semantic labels, 90.4\% of system-effect weight falls
452	into mixed buckets. A flat \texttt{cargo~test} counter shows 2{,}903
453	executions but cannot distinguish whether they came from
454	\texttt{review}, \texttt{debug}, \texttt{refactor}, or \texttt{test}
455	prompts. Adding only the prompt label reduces mixed weight to 36.7\% and
456	residual to 7.5\%. The session label alone barely helps (84.4\%), because
457	sessions typically contain multiple intent phases.
458	
459	A concrete example illustrates the scale. \texttt{process:cargo; effect:test; status:ok}
460	appears under 48 distinct prompt labels. The top label (\texttt{refactor})
461	accounts for only 32.0\%; the remaining 68.0\% comes from
462	\texttt{review}, \texttt{research}, \texttt{test}, \texttt{explain}, and
463	others. A flat summary or process audit merges all of these.
464	
465	As a robustness check, a label-permutation test (1{,}000 shuffles within
466	each session) confirms the separation is not random ($p = 0.001$). This
467	result assumes label quality, a dependency we validate in RQ3 for
468	structured traces (V-measure above 0.7 on 7/9 datasets). For the
469	regex-derived labels on real sessions, the permutation test confirms
470	non-random separation, but direct quality assessment against
471	human-annotated ground truth remains future work.
472	
473	RQ1 also tests whether query-time stack selection (R2) adds value
474	beyond flat label grouping. The same two-abstraction model covers all 15
475	public trace families (Table~\ref{tab:datasets}) without type-specific
476	objects. On the four oracle-rich families, the same 13{,}265 operations
477	fold from 9~dataset stacks to 57~phase stacks, 226~semantic stacks,
478	455~action stacks, or 3{,}757~fixed-session stacks by changing only the
479	stack fields. A flat GROUP BY on a single label cannot produce these views because
480	different stack depths answer different questions (task-level
481	budget vs.\ action-level duplication vs.\ session-level drilldown), and
482	the profiler produces all of them from the same operations.
483	
484	The multi-view design is further validated by metric divergence. The
485	\texttt{time} and \texttt{tokens} views of the same sessions share
486	only 7/10 top prompt categories (Spearman $\rho = 0.623$).
487	\texttt{network}-tagged prompts rank 8th by time (I/O wait) but 93rd by
488	tokens.
489	
490	These quantitative results translate to concrete aggregate insights.
491	The \texttt{tokens} view (Figure~\ref{fig:flamegraphs}) reveals that
492	\texttt{review}-tagged prompts dominate the model budget, followed by
493	\texttt{git}, \texttt{code}, \texttt{edit}, and \texttt{debug}. A timeline of 80{,}000 individual LLM calls cannot
494	produce this distribution without external aggregation. The \texttt{files} view shows
495	\texttt{debug}-tagged prompts across different sessions repeatedly
496	accessing the same source files, aggregated into a single wide bar that
497	a timeline shows as isolated events. The \texttt{network} view
498	attributes domain contacts to prompt categories, and the \texttt{files}
499	view identifies accesses outside the project root, supporting security
500	auditing.
501	
502	\begin{figure}[t]
503	\centering
504	% \includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/flamegraph-tokens.png}
505	\fbox{\parbox{0.93\linewidth}{\centering\small
506	[Flame-graph screenshots: tokens view (top) and files view (bottom)
507	showing budget distribution and file-access patterns across sessions]}}
508	\caption{Real flame graphs from a development project.
509	Top: \texttt{tokens} view (width = token count).
510	Bottom: \texttt{files} view (width = file-operation count).}
511	\Description{Two flame graphs showing token budget and file access
512	distribution across semantic prompt categories.}
513	\label{fig:flamegraphs}
514	\end{figure}
515	
516	%% -------------------------------------------------------------------
517	\subsection{RQ2: Can Profiler Groups Localize Hidden Labeled Problems?}
518	
519	RQ2 asks whether the profiler's top groups correspond to real labeled
520	problems, specifically whether categories that concentrate failures, safety
521	violations, or wasted effort surface at the top of ranked output. The
522	methodology is analogous to injecting known
523	bottlenecks in a CPU profiler evaluation. Public benchmark datasets
524	provide ground-truth labels (failure, safety violation, redundant step,
525	human-task boundary); we hide these labels, run the profiler, rank the
526	resulting groups, and check whether the top groups contain the hidden
527	positives.
528	
529	\paragraph{Benchmark setup.}
530	The benchmark uses six tasks across four datasets (AgentRewardBench
531	looping and side-effect, SATraj-OS unsafe operation, AgentNet incorrect
532	and redundant step, and OSWorld-Human group start), totaling 34{,}539 operations and
533	3{,}699 positives. Six views (flat, fixed-session, dataset-native,
534	raw-action, operation-stack, label-drilldown) and four rankers (width,
535	visible-risk, query-aware, oracle).
536	
537	\paragraph{Localization results.}
538	
539	\begin{table*}[t]
540	\centering\small
541	\caption{RQ2 hidden-label localization (medians across six tasks).
542	Hidden policies serve only as upper bounds. WTFP = work-to-first-positive.
543	``---'' = group count varies by task; no single median is reported.}
544	\label{tab:localization}
545	\begin{tabular}{lrrrrrrrr}
546	\toprule
547	Policy & Hidden & AP & R@5 & F1@5 & Work@5 & R@30\% & WTFP & Groups \\
548	\midrule
549	flat:width & 0 & 0.168 & 1.000 & 0.287 & 1.000 & 0.000 & 1.000 & 1.0 \\
550	fixed-session:query-aware & 0 & 0.348 & 0.023 & 0.043 & 0.016 & 0.356 & 0.004 & 285.0 \\
551	dataset-native:query-aware & 0 & 0.357 & 0.867 & 0.282 & 0.854 & 0.338 & 0.058 & --- \\
552	raw-action:query-aware & 0 & 0.274 & 0.244 & 0.220 & 0.151 & 0.333 & 0.037 & --- \\
553	op-stack:query-aware & 0 & 0.312 & 0.188 & 0.198 & 0.094 & 0.390 & 0.038 & 157.5 \\
554	op-stack:oracle-upper & 1 & 0.599 & 0.300 & 0.403 & 0.044 & 0.564 & 0.012 & --- \\
555	label-drilldown:oracle & 1 & 1.000 & 0.670 & 0.797 & 0.115 & 1.000 & 0.038 & --- \\
556	\bottomrule
557	\end{tabular}
558	\end{table*}
559	
560	Table~\ref{tab:localization} summarizes the results. Flat summaries
561	recover all positives but require inspecting everything
562	(Work@5\,=\,1.0). Fixed-session drilldown finds a first positive quickly
563	(WTFP\,=\,0.004) but fragments the workload into 285 groups with only
564	2.3\% top-five recall. Operation-stack query-aware profiling inspects
565	9.4\% of the work in the top five groups, achieves 39.0\% budget-30
566	recall, and reduces groups to 157.5.
567	
568	The result is a Pareto tradeoff, not dominance. The comparison also
569	serves as evidence for the two-abstraction model (\S\ref{sec:design}). Fixed-session
570	drilldown and dataset-native hierarchy are alternative abstractions that
571	fix the hierarchy at session or dataset boundaries. Operation stacks
572	subsume both as special cases (include \texttt{session} in the stack
573	to recover fixed-session; include \texttt{dataset} to recover
574	dataset-native). On localization, operation stacks improve top-five
575	recall over fixed-session on 5/6 tasks, reduce median group count by
576	45\%, and save 90\% of inspection work versus flat summaries.
577	Fixed-session drilldown retains lower work-to-first-positive on 4/6
578	tasks, confirming that profilers and debuggers are complementary.
579	
580	Statistical validation supports these comparisons. Bootstrap
581	(10{,}000 resamples) and label-permutation (2{,}000 trials) confirm
582	stable AP deltas exceeding the 95\% prevalence/group-size null on all
583	six tasks.
584	
585	\paragraph{Actionability: which configuration knobs explain the results?}
586	
587	Executable profile-spec patches modify stack fields, mapping rules, or
588	rankers, then re-run over the same visible operations. Five of six
589	patches improve AP, top-five lift, and first-positive work (median AP
590	delta 0.038, median top-five lift delta 0.575). Three reusable patterns
591	emerge: (1)~safety/side-effect tasks benefit from field and ranker
592	changes; (2)~step-quality tasks benefit from operation-stack
593	localization followed by fixed-session drilldown for examples;
594	(3)~human-boundary tasks require boundary-derived fields. The rejected
595	OSWorld-Human patch shows that visible rank features alone are
596	insufficient for boundary objectives; folding held-out boundary-derived
597	fields improves AP from 0.240 to 0.258 and reduces groups from 108 to
598	74, with an explicit work tradeoff.
599	
600	Rank-feature ablations identify 7 critical feature rows
601	(\texttt{repeat\_signal}, write-action, \texttt{status=success}) and 3
602	misleading rows. Guided repairs improve AP on 2/3 misleading cases but
603	use offline scored feedback, not an automatic learned ranker.
604	
605	%% -------------------------------------------------------------------
606	\subsection{RQ3: How Reliable Is Intent Recognition?}
607	
608	RQ1 and RQ2 assume that semantic labels are useful. RQ3 tests the
609	label-derivation pipeline itself. For structured traces (public
610	datasets), we evaluate the \emph{mapping} path against ground-truth
611	annotations. For free-form traces (real sessions), we evaluate the
612	\emph{intent-recognition} path at the scale and syntax level. Quality
613	assessment of the LLM/regex tagger against free-form ground truth
614	remains future work.
615	
616	\paragraph{Scale and syntax validity.}
617	On 325 real sessions, the LLM tagger processes 118{,}021 tag requests
618	(2{,}859 prompt rows, 114{,}837 LLM-call events), of which 82{,}886 hit
619	the label cache and 35{,}136 require real llama.cpp calls to a local
620	3B-parameter model. All requests complete without tag failures. On a
621	fixed set of 300 redacted fragments, three model sizes (0.6B, 1.1B, 3B)
622	all produce 900/900 syntactically valid outputs with p95 latencies of
623	23, 18, and 31\,ms respectively.
624	
625	\paragraph{Ground-truth agreement on public datasets.}
626	Public benchmark datasets provide native action labels that serve as
627	ground truth for mapping quality. We run a leave-dataset-out evaluation.
628	For each of 9 datasets, we train mapping rules on the other 8 and
629	measure V-measure between the mapping-derived \texttt{phase} field and
630	the dataset's native \texttt{action} labels, plus boundary F1 between
631	mapped phase boundaries and native action boundaries.
632	
633	\begin{table}[t]
634	\centering\small
635	\caption{Leave-dataset-out mapping quality. V-measure between
636	mapping-derived \texttt{phase} and native \texttt{action} labels.
637	13{,}265 operations from the four oracle-rich families
638	across 9 held-out evaluations.}
639	\label{tab:vmeasure}
640	\begin{tabular}{lrrr}
641	\toprule
642	Held-out dataset & Ops & V-measure & Boundary F1 \\
643	\midrule
644	mind2web & 774 & 1.000 & 1.000 \\
645	webshop-expert & 2{,}504 & 1.000 & 1.000 \\
646	swe-agent & 496 & 0.926 & 0.962 \\
647	weblinx-chat & 500 & 0.872 & 0.860 \\
648	agenttrek & 200 & 0.862 & --- \\
649	gui-odyssey & 7{,}868 & 0.811 & 0.842 \\
650	android-control & 9 & 0.716 & 0.727 \\
651	toolbench & 866 & 0.134 & 0.353 \\
652	api-bank & 48 & 0.000 & --- \\
653	\bottomrule
654	\end{tabular}
655	\end{table}
656	
657	Table~\ref{tab:vmeasure} shows the results. On 7/9 datasets, V-measure
658	exceeds 0.7, indicating strong agreement between mapping-derived and
659	native labels. The two low-scoring datasets (toolbench, api-bank) have
660	atypical action vocabularies that the held-out mapping rules do not
661	cover. Mapping reduces unique stacks on 6/9 datasets with zero negative
662	regressions.
663	
664	A supervised boundary-derivation backend further validates the field
665	pipeline. On OSWorld-Human held-out adjacent pairs, a learned boundary
666	predictor achieves F1~0.77, beating the best simple baseline
667	(\texttt{always\_boundary}, F1~0.71). Learned backends beat simple
668	baselines on 4/5 tested boundary families, while AgentRewardBench
669	looping is fully explained by \texttt{repeat\_signal\_change} (baseline
670	F1~1.0). These baseline comparisons support field derivation as a guarded configuration
671	step, not automatic intent discovery.
672	
673	Two mapping-rule variants (differing in API/tool phase precedence) run
674	on the same 13{,}265 operations and produce identical V-measure on 7/9
675	datasets, with the two divergent datasets differing by $\leq$0.17.
676	Mapping quality is robust to minor rule variations on well-covered
677	action vocabularies. Direct cross-backend comparison between the regex
678	and LLM taggers on the same free-form prompts remains future work.
679	
680	Syntactic validity does not imply semantic quality. TinyLlama 1.1B
681	achieves high exact-stability (279/300 identical across repeats) but
682	concentrates on a narrow label set. The 3B model produces a broader
683	vocabulary (328 unique prompt labels) but includes noisy entries. A
684	display-governance pipeline reduces unique labels from 1{,}546 to
685	1{,}364 through deterministic aliases, raising top-20 support coverage
686	from 93.7\% to 95.2\% without overwriting raw labels. This pipeline manages
687	noise but does not establish semantic adequacy. The ground-truth and
688	cross-backend checks above provide that.
689	
690	All results are backed by profile specs for deterministic replay. We
691	re-execute 76 tracked specs twice (152 invocations), and all produce
692	identical output with median runtime 1.6\,s per spec.
693	
694	%% ===================================================================
695	\section{Related Work}
696	
697	\textbf{Profiling and flame graphs.}
698	Flame graphs~\cite{flamegraphs} and pprof~\cite{pprof} establish the
699	folded-stack lineage. Profiles are weighted samples with location
700	hierarchies. Pprof supports sample labels and can visualize them as
701	pseudo stack frames through tag-root/tag-leaf options. Perfetto
702	generalizes trace ingestion with SQL-based analysis and derived
703	events~\cite{perfetto}. These systems support query-time aggregation, so
704	\toolname does not claim novelty for flexible aggregation alone. The
705	difference is the domain. Samples are agent operations, frames are
706	semantic labels derived from natural-language prompts through intent
707	recognition, and the evaluation scores profiler output against hidden
708	agent-trajectory labels.
709	
710	\textbf{Agent tracing and LLM observability.}
711	OpenTelemetry GenAI and OpenInference standardize GenAI
712	spans~\cite{otel, openinference}. LangSmith~\cite{langsmith},
713	Langfuse~\cite{langfuse}, and Phoenix~\cite{phoenix} provide trace
714	visualization, session management, evaluations, and dashboards.
715	AgentOps~\cite{agentops} argues for structured agent observability
716	covering goals, plans, tools, and artifacts. These systems excel at
717	single-execution debugging. \toolname complements them with cross-session
718	aggregate profiling. Datadog LLM Observability and Laminar Signals take
719	steps toward semantic aggregation by clustering user messages or
720	extracting structured events, but they characterize \emph{input
721	distributions}, not \emph{resource attribution}.
722	
723	\textbf{Agent failure diagnosis.}
724	AgentRx~\cite{agentrx} releases annotated failure trajectories and uses
725	constraint checking plus an LLM judge for root-cause localization.
726	TELBench~\cite{telbench} builds span-localization benchmarks from
727	semantic error annotations. AgentAtlas~\cite{agentatlas} argues that outcome leaderboards
728	miss trajectory-level quality. These systems perform \emph{span-level}
729	fault localization within a single execution: which step failed and why.
730	\toolname performs \emph{category-level} aggregate profiling, identifying
731	which categories of work produce the most failures, consume the most
732	budget, or generate repeated system effects across sessions.
733	
734	%% ===================================================================
735	\section{Conclusion}
736	
737	Agent observability needs profiling, not only debugging. The obstacle is
738	that natural-language prompts lack the deterministic identifiers that
739	make flame-graph folding work. \toolname shows that two
740	abstractions, operations and operation stacks, close this gap once
741	intent recognition restores deterministic labels. The evaluation
742	confirms that semantic profiling separates information that flat views merge,
743	localizes labeled problems with less work than both flat summaries and
744	fixed-session drilldown, and produces labels that agree with
745	ground-truth annotations across heterogeneous public datasets.
746	
747	Profilers and debuggers are complementary. Fixed-session drilldown finds
748	a first positive faster on 4/6 tasks (RQ2), while the profiler
749	identifies which categories deserve attention. \toolname supports both
750	by including or excluding session fields in the stack query. The
751	profiler's structured output (JSON, pprof, folded stacks) is designed
752	for automated consumption by analysis agents, though evaluation of
753	agent-driven diagnosis is future work.
754	
755	The main limitation is single-project real-session data. Multi-project
756	evaluation and trace-ecosystem integration (importing OpenTelemetry and
757	LangSmith traces as operations) are the most impactful next steps.
758

\newcommand{\toolname}{\textsc{AgentPProf}\xspace}
\newcommand{\operation}{\texttt{operation}\xspace}
\newcommand{\opstack}{\texttt{operation stack}\xspace}

\begin{document}

\title{AgentPProf: Semantic Profiling for AI Agent Traces}

\begin{abstract}
AI agents produce complex execution traces spanning prompts, LLM calls,
tool invocations, GUI actions, and system effects. As deployments grow
to hundreds of sessions, both human operators and automated analysis
pipelines need aggregate views, not just per-execution debugging.
Existing observability tools organize events into fixed session/span
hierarchies suited for single-run debugging but unable to fold events
across sessions by semantic work category.
We show that agent profiling reduces to two abstractions once intent
recognition restores the deterministic-label precondition that
flame-graph folding requires.
An \emph{operation} is a uniform weighted record for any agent activity.
An \emph{operation stack} is a field projection chosen at query time.
\toolname implements this model with pluggable intent-recognition
backends (regex rules, local LLM tagging, unsupervised clustering) and
produces flame graphs, pprof profiles, and structured JSON consumable by
both developers and analysis agents.
On 325 real agent sessions, semantic labels separate 90\% of
system-effect weight that flat views merge. On six localization tasks across four public datasets
(34{,}539 operations), operation-stack profiling reduces inspection work
by 90\% versus flat summaries and group fragmentation by 45\% versus
fixed-session drilldown. On 7/9 held-out datasets, leave-dataset-out mapping achieves V-measure
above 0.7.
\end{abstract}

\maketitle

%% ===================================================================
\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:intro}

%% ¶1: Background + Context
AI agent systems produce heterogeneous execution traces spanning
prompts, LLM calls, tool invocations, GUI actions, and system effects.
As deployments scale to hundreds of sessions and tens of thousands of
calls, both developers and automated analysis agents need aggregate
views, including which categories of work consume the most tokens, where
failures concentrate, and how cost distributes across semantic task
families.

%% ¶2: Problem + example
However, no existing observability tool folds events across sessions
into an aggregate cost distribution. LangSmith~\cite{langsmith},
Langfuse~\cite{langfuse}, Phoenix~\cite{phoenix}, and OpenTelemetry
GenAI~\cite{otel} organize events into per-execution timelines and
span trees, enabling single-run debugging but not cross-session
aggregation. In a real development project, the system effect
\texttt{process:cargo; effect:test; status:ok} appears 2{,}903 times
across 325 sessions, yet no existing trace tool can disaggregate these
executions by the semantic intent that triggered them.

%% ¶3: Root cause
CPU profilers solved the equivalent aggregation problem for programs.
Flame graphs~\cite{flamegraphs} fold millions of function-call samples
into a single chart where width represents cost. The key enabler is
\emph{deterministic} function names that merge identical call stacks.
Agent traces break this precondition because prompts are natural
language, and
two prompts expressing the same intent share no characters
(\S\ref{sec:background}).

%% ¶4: Existing solutions fail
Some existing tools take steps toward semantic grouping. Datadog LLM
Observability clusters user messages by
topic,\footnote{\url{https://docs.datadoghq.com/llm_observability/}}
and Laminar extracts structured signals from
traces.\footnote{\url{https://docs.lmnr.ai/signals/introduction}} Both characterize \emph{input distributions} (``30\% of users ask code
questions'') but not \emph{resource attribution} (``code-review tasks
consume 40\% of the token budget'').

%% ¶5: Key insight
We observe that agent observability requires \emph{semantic profiling},
meaning aggregate, cross-session cost attribution grouped by user
intent, as distinct from execution-structural groupings like sessions or
spans. The obstacle is the nondeterminism of natural-language identifiers.
Intent recognition can restore deterministic labels, making semantic
profiling tractable.

%% ¶6: This paper + numbers
This paper presents \toolname, a profiler that restores aggregate
flame-graph analysis for agent traces. The profiler is built on two
abstractions: an \emph{operation} (a uniform weighted record for any
agent activity) and an \emph{operation stack} (a field projection chosen
at query time). \toolname recovers the deterministic-label precondition through
\emph{intent recognition}, which maps free-form prompts to stable labels
using pluggable backends (regex rules, local LLM tagging, or
unsupervised clustering). On 325 real sessions, semantic labels separate
90\% of system-effect weight that flat views merge. On four public
datasets,
operation-stack profiling reduces inspection work by 90\% versus flat
summaries.

%% ¶7: Contributions
This paper makes three contributions:

  We show that fixed session/span hierarchies cannot fold by semantic

\section{Background and Motivation}
\label{sec:background}

\subsection{How Existing Agent Trace Models Work}

Current agent observability tools organize traces around fixed
hierarchies. OpenTelemetry represents an execution as a \emph{trace}
containing a tree of \emph{spans}, each with a name, duration, and
key-value attributes. LangSmith and Langfuse group spans into
\emph{sessions} and display them as timelines or waterfall charts.
Phoenix and OpenInference add GenAI-specific span types for LLM calls,
tool invocations, retrieval steps, and agent reasoning.

These models share a structural property, namely that the session or
span tree is the skeleton of the data. Every event belongs to exactly one span, and
spans nest in a fixed parent-child hierarchy determined at execution
time. This design is effective for debugging because a developer can
locate a failing span, inspect its attributes, and trace its parent
chain to understand the execution context.

\subsection{Why Fixed Hierarchies Cannot Profile}

Profiling requires a fundamentally different operation, \emph{folding}
events across executions by semantic category so that width represents
aggregate cost. Fixed session/span hierarchies obstruct this in three
ways.

First, sessions are boundaries, not categories. A single session may
contain review, debugging, and refactoring phases, and splitting by
session assigns all of them to the same bucket. Conversely, two sessions
performing the same task produce separate buckets that cannot be merged
without external logic. Second, span names describe mechanisms
(\texttt{LLMCall}, \texttt{ToolInvoke}, \texttt{ChatCompletion}), not
user intent (\texttt{review}, \texttt{debug}, \texttt{test}). Grouping
by span name tells you how many LLM calls occurred, not which categories
of work consumed the budget. Third, these limitations compound in practice. A common system effect
like running a test suite may appear thousands of times across sessions,
but a flat process summary shows only a single counter with no way to
attribute executions to the semantic intent that triggered them. We
quantify this disaggregation in RQ1~(\S\ref{sec:eval}).

\subsection{Why CPU Profiling Does Not Directly Apply}

CPU profilers solve the equivalent aggregation problem for programs.
A flame graph~\cite{flamegraphs} represents a profile as a set of
weighted \emph{samples}, each attached to a \emph{call stack} (an
ordered list of function frames). Identical stacks merge, and width
represents aggregate cost. The key enabler is that function names are
\emph{deterministic}. The same code path always produces the same
frames.

Agent traces break this precondition. Prompts are natural language and
lack deterministic identifiers. Tool calls, GUI
actions, and process events are named heterogeneously across agent
families. Raw event names cannot serve as flame-graph frames.

These observations yield three design requirements:

\begin{description}
\item[R1: Uniform record type.]
  Agent traces mix prompts, LLM calls, tool invocations, GUI actions,
  process events, and benchmark labels. The profiler needs a single
  record type that can represent all of them without type-specific
  objects.
\item[R2: Query-time aggregation.]
  The same data must support multiple aggregation shapes (by task,
  phase, action, session, or dataset) without rebuilding the trace.
  Sessions and spans must be fields, not fixed hierarchy nodes.
\item[R3: Deterministic labels for folding.]
  Free-form prompts must be mapped to short, stable, repeatable labels
  before folding. This \emph{intent recognition} step has no analogue in
  CPU profiling, where function names are already deterministic.
\end{description}
